ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 et seq., specifically L.561-2-2 (beneficial owner definition), L.561-10 (PEP due diligence), L.561-15 (TRACFIN reporting), L.561-45 to L.561-48 (beneficial ownership register); Code de commerce, Articles L.123-23 et seq. (RCS); Décret n°2018-284 and Ordonnance n°2020-115 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; RBE procedural rules under CMF R.561-20 et seq.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of passport bio-data page and current proof of residential address of each proposed SARL manager and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public or competent passport issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / equivalent Registrar extract for any foreign corporate shareholder of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies or competent corporate register in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the origin country is not an Apostille Convention member, French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the French incorporation agent or local counsel to complete RCS filing and sign incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent corporate authority in the shareholder's or manager's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization, as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, and significant counterparties against the EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, French national asset-freeze decrees issued by the Direction générale du Trésor, and, because of USD-denominated LME copper arbitrage, the U.S. OFAC SDN list. PEP status must be assessed under CMF Article L.561-10. Suspicious transactions and attempted transactions must be reported to TRACFIN under CMF Article L.561-15. A negative screening report, source-of-wealth explanation, and record-retention undertaking of at least five years must be completed before RCS filing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (procedures.inpi.fr); name availability verified through data.inpi.fr and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be capable of being registered in Latin script. French-language statuts and registration declarations are mandatory. If a proposed name originates in a non-Latin script, an official Latin-script transliteration must be filed and will constitute the operative registered name. Foreign commercial terms may be used, but the registrar may require a French explanatory form where a name could mislead as to activity or legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may: (1) obtain the written rejection reason from the Guichet Unique or the registrar; (2) file an administrative reconsideration request with the same registry within 15 days from notification; (3) if the rejection is upheld, commence summary proceedings before the President of the competent Tribunal judiciaire or Tribunal de commerce within one month of notification; (4) alternatively, refile using a distinctive suffix or modified denomination. Renewal of an INPI-issued name reservation requires a new reservation application submitted before expiry of the 5-year period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SARL is permitted to use a virtual registered office through a duly authorised company domiciliation provider under Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce. A PO Box alone is not acceptable. For wholesale copper cathode trading and LC/LME warrant payment rails, banks and AML obliged entities will typically require a demonstrated administrative substance, such as a French correspondence address, local director/manager substance, or accounting records in France. Virtual office acceptance is therefore conditional and subject to enhanced KYC review for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10-15% probability of an unannounced inspection or substance verification within the first 24 months of registration; the risk rises to approximately 25% if the SARL has non-resident managers, no staff, and only mailbox domiciliation while conducting high-volume physical commodity arbitrage.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-36 governing SARLs; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing registration and commercial formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités, with review and registration by the competent Registry of the Commercial Court (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of incorporation (declaration de constitution) submitted electronically through the Guichet unique, together with the signed SARL articles of association and supporting documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required; EUR 1 is generally sufficient. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des depots before filing, and the deposit certificate must be submitted. The blocked funds are released after issuance of the registration extract (Kbis).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders, acting as the first governing body of the Company, resolve that the subscribed capital of EUR [amount], divided into [number] shares of EUR [value] each, is approved and shall be paid in accordance with the articles. The registered office is established at [full French address]. [Name, address, and nationality] is appointed Manager (Gerant) for the statutory term and accepts the appointment. The Manager is authorized to complete incorporation filings, publish the legal notice, open and operate the Company bank account, and execute all documents required for registration and commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate identity, activities, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalites; competent Commercial Court Registry for the registered-office location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the corporate name, verify availability, determine the principal activity as wholesale trading of refined copper cathodes, and secure a lawful French registered office. Obtain written domicile consent or a lease, domiciliation agreement, or premises title. The activity is generally commercial and does not require a sector-specific trading license.
required_dossiers: Business activity description and applicable NAF code
Identification details of shareholders and Manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace or qualify the corporate name, correct the activity description, or provide supplementary office evidence before filing. A registry objection should be answered through the Guichet unique within the stated correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SARL articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution by shareholders; notarial intervention only where legally required, including qualifying real-estate contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles in French, specifying corporate name, form, purpose, registered office, duration, capital, share allocation, transfer restrictions, Manager appointment method, and accounting year. Have all shareholders sign the articles. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary cash contributions; certified translations may be used for foreign-language documents.
required_dossiers: Shareholder powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct statutory omissions, execution defects, or translation deficiencies and re-sign the affected pages. Obtain a notarial deed if an in-kind contribution or real-estate transfer requires it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, French notary, or Caisse des depots
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital-deposit account, transfer at least 20% of each cash subscription, and submit the signed articles, shareholder identification, Manager identification, and source-of-funds documentation. Obtain the capital deposit certificate. The remaining cash capital must be paid within five years after registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank compliance requests, replace incomplete identification documents, or use a French notary or Caisse des depots if the bank declines onboarding. No capital release should occur before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French legal-announcement publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a legal notice of incorporation containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, Manager identity, and registration details. Pay the regulated publication charge and obtain the publication certificate or notice receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if the notice contains an error. Retain both the original and corrected publication certificates for the registration file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic company-formation form, upload the signed articles, registered-office evidence, publication certificate, capital deposit certificate, Manager declaration, identity documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. Sign electronically, pay the registry and beneficial-owner charges, and monitor the filing dashboard.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer any INPI or Registry query through the electronic portal, upload corrected documents, and resubmit within the prescribed deadline. If rejected, correct the stated defect and file a new or amended application; judicial review or a registry complaint may be considered where procedurally appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry, INPI, tax administration, and social-security bodies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN/SIRET numbers, Kbis extract, and definitive beneficial-owner filing confirmation. Request release of deposited capital, complete bank onboarding, register for VAT and corporate tax obligations, establish accounting records, and enroll employees with the relevant social-security bodies before hiring.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate delayed registration through the Registry or INPI support channels, correct tax-registration inconsistencies with the relevant tax office, and postpone regulated physical operations until premises and safety approvals are complete.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sector-specific industrial licensing board applies to ordinary wholesale trading of Grade A refined copper cathodes. For storage facilities or environmentally regulated installations, the competent authority is the relevant Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (Direction regionale de l'environnement, de l'amenagement et du logement; DREAL), or DRIEAT in the Paris region.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or commodity-trading operating permit. A site-specific declaration, registration, or authorization under the Classified Installations for Environmental Protection regime (ICPE) may be required for storage, waste handling, combustion equipment, or other regulated installations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Regional Directorate for Environment, Planning and Housing (Direction regionale de l'environnement, de l'amenagement et du logement; DREAL), or DRIEAT for Ile-de-France
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not automatically required for ordinary wholesale trading without processing. A project-specific screening applies under the French Environmental Code; an ICPE declaration, registration, authorization, or environmental assessment may be triggered by warehouse size, storage characteristics, waste status, emissions, or construction works.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industry-wide copper-trading threshold applies. Any wastewater discharge must comply with the applicable Environmental Code provisions and local discharge authorization, including pollutant limits imposed by the permit. Atmospheric emissions, including VOCs, are regulated only where relevant equipment or substances are present. Copper-bearing or hazardous waste must be segregated, transferred to authorized operators, documented through required traceability records, and managed under applicable waste-classification rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupation, the warehouse should satisfy applicable fire-safety and public-access requirements, including emergency exits, extinguishers, fire detection, compartmentation, access for emergency services, and storage-risk controls. Structural capacity and floor loading must be verified for cathode and pallet loads. The employer must complete occupational-risk assessment, prevention measures, worker training, personal protective equipment, handling procedures, and workplace inspections. A formal fire or occupational clearance is conditional on the premises classification and does not replace any required building, ICPE, or local-authority approval.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) is the French tax administration responsible for corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding taxes. Its digital portal is impots.gouv.fr and the dedicated professional online portal is www.impots.gouv.fr. The Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) handles customs controls and export/import declarations, and collaborates with the DGFiP for export zero-rating evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL incorporated by foreign shareholders, the legal representative completes the single online registration at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique). The registration dossier triggers the issuance by INSEE of a SIREN (9-digit) and SIRET (14-digit), and the Tax Office automatically allocates the VAT intra-community number (FR+11 digits). A foreign entity not yet registered in France but making taxable supplies must apply directly to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) using Form Cerfa n°1547-M, accompanied by statutory documents (constitutive documents, identity of directors, evidence of economic activity). Non-EU entities are generally required to appoint a tax representative approved by the tax authority before registration is effective.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Under Article 239 bis AA of the French General Tax Code (CGI), a small SARL with fewer than 50 employees and annual turnover below certain thresholds may elect to be transparent for income tax purposes (i.e., taxed under impôt sur le revenu as an entity for five fiscal years). Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD are mandatory; Article 212 ter CGI disallows deduction of payments involving hybrid instruments or hybrid entities, with no elective 'choose-your-own' classification. A SARL can alternatively be treated as a partnership for income tax purposes only in limited family-run situations, but the default status is corporate tax (IS).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for a French-established taxable person; VAT registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply. The small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base) applies to turnover below €85,000 per year for supplies of goods and €37,500 for services, but such businesses may opt to become VAT-registered. For sellers from another EU Member State to French private consumers, the €10,000 distance-sales threshold applies, after which French VAT must be charged and remitted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: DGFiP will phase in mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting in France. Obligated companies must use a certified Dematerialization Partner Platform (PDP) or the public Chorus Pro portal. The current timetable is September 1, 2026 for large and mid-sized companies and September 1, 2027 for small and micro-enterprises. Invoices must be submitted in structured formats (Factur-X, UBL or compatible formats) and transaction data (supplier/purchaser VAT IDs, invoice dates and amounts, payment terms) are reported to DGFiP in near real-time. France does not use pre-approval digital stamping; it operates a 'continuous transaction controls' model with mandatory e-reporting of all business-to-business and business-to-consumer transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of Grade A copper cathodes to customers outside the European Union are zero-rated for VAT under Article 262-I-1° of the CGI, provided that the exporter proves that the goods have been dispatched or transported outside the EU, supports the movement with an export customs declaration (lodged via DELTA/EAS systems), and retains transport documents (bill of lading, CMR or air waybill). Intra-Community supplies to taxable purchasers in another EU Member State are also zero-rated under Article 256 bis CGI if the purchaser is VAT-registered and the goods are physically moved to that State; the supplier must hold a valid EU VAT ID and submit the recapitulative statement (DEB). Since copper cathodes are a commodity, the mere transaction on LME warrants without physical movement is not allowable for export zero-rating; physical export must be substantiated. Services directly related to the export or transport of these goods may also be zero-rated if the recipient is established outside the EU or is an EU trader in the case of intra-community services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (déclaration d'exportation) lodged electronically via DELTA or ECS system
Bill of Lading (or equivalent transport document such as CMR or waybill) evidencing the movement leaving French and EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT confirmation proving receipt of the export proceeds in France within 180 days
Commercial invoice issued by the French supplier and accepted by the non-EU or EU customer
Packing list for the copper cathode consignments
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French customs and tax authorities apply strict cross-checking between the export declaration (DELTA), the transport documents and the export proceeds ledger. If the zero-rating is successfully challenged, the company is liable for the unpaid VAT plus late interest and penalties up to 80% for fraud (manoeuvres frauduleuses). Customs penalties for false export declarations can reach 1.5 to 3 times the evaded duties/taxes, and the Douanes may also impose customs detention and administrative fines. The controller may retrospectively disallow input VAT recovered in relation to the export if the documentation is incomplete or if the transaction is reclassified as a domestic or intra-union supply without reimbursement. Failure to provide evidence within the six-year records retention period or inability to demonstrate actual payment repatriation can lead to accounts reassessment, tax liens, and professional interdiction in serious fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting in coordination with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking and prudential supervision, the Direction Générale du Trésor within the French Ministry of Economy and Finance for balance-of-payments and foreign-investment screening, and the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for customs and trade-statistics requirements. The legal bases are the Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 (EMIR), the EU anti-money-laundering framework implemented in the CMF, and the free-movement-of-capital provisions of Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full legal and practical convertibility of the euro (EUR) and all major currencies, including the US Dollar (USD), for both current-account and capital-account transactions. No French exchange-control authorisation is required to open a USD account, convert export proceeds into EUR, remit dividends or interest to non-resident shareholders, repay intra-group loans, or repatriate liquidation proceeds. Eurozone membership and the EU capital-mobility guarantees under Article 63 TFEU effectively eliminate any material distinction between current and capital account convertibility for a French SARL. The residual regulatory burdens are procedural and statistical: (i) resident companies carrying out material cross-border operations must file balance-of-payments and external-position declarations with the Banque de France under the SAFE reporting system when annual external flows cross the applicable de minimis thresholds; (ii) loans from non-resident shareholders must be declared as external indebtedness to the Banque de France; and (iii) foreign investment in a French company operating in a sensitive sector may require prior approval under the IEF procedure, a regime that does not apply to wholesale copper-cathode trading. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are freely transferable in the currency of distribution; taxation under the French General Tax Code and double-tax treaties is separate from, and does not condition, the foreign-exchange transfer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender ratio, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no requirement to convert export proceeds into EUR or deposit them with a French bank. A copper-cathode trading SARL may retain 100% of export proceeds in USD or any convertible currency indefinitely and may deploy those proceeds directly to fund upstream purchases, post hedge collateral, or service shareholder obligations. The only obligations are declarative and documentary: (i) monthly or quarterly balance-of-payments and external-financial-position declarations to the Banque de France when annual goods or financial flows cross the SAFE reporting thresholds, commonly observed at EUR 15 million of annual external goods flows for active trading entities; (ii) Intrastat declarations for intra-EU acquisitions and supplies, plus DGDDI customs export declarations and the EU Customs Security Filing for physical shipments; and (iii) the mandatory transmission of full originator and beneficiary information under the EU Funds Transfer Regulation in every SWIFT payment. No ministry approval, surrender certificate, or FX conversion receipt is required for the export of Grade A refined copper cathodes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account (compte courant) in EUR plus segregated USD clearing account and trade-finance facility for documentary credits, LME warrant settlements and warehouse financing
Operational current account in EUR/USD plus structured commodity trade finance (LC issuance, receivables purchase, inventory financing) and global-markets FX coverage

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (CACIB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational corporate account, EUR and USD clearing, metals and mining commodity finance desk, escrow and lockbox structures for LME warrant transfers
Operational account, commodity trade finance (pre-export financing, LC and standby issuance), FX and commodity derivatives under ISDA/EMIR, USD correspondent clearing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, consolidated by the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months following the closing of the fiscal year; extended to eight (8) months during the first fiscal year of the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 1,000 (EUR 500 for entities with single natural-person shareholder); increased to EUR 3,000 for second-late filing within a five-year period; publication of the court order possible; continued delinquency may trigger civil liability and judicial strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Beneficial Ownership (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet Unique (via the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle - INPI), transmitted to the RCS and the RNE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within fifteen (15) days of the anniversary date of the filing of the original declaration to the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 130 per company for late filing or non-filing; potential criminal sanctions of imprisonment of six months and/or fine of EUR 15,000 for intentionally failing to file or for providing false information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social and Tax Declaration of Corporate Income Tax (Déclaration de Résultats - N° 2065 / 2065-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day following 1 May of the year following the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the net tax due (or 40% in case of deliberate non-filing); interest at the statutory rate of 5% for late payment; in extreme cases, administrative penalties and enforced recovery.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation of Exercise of Tax Option (Impôt sur les Sociétés vs. Impôt sur le Revenu) - Annual Declaration of Tax Result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual corporate income tax return (within the statutory filing window set by the DGFIP, generally by the second business day following 1 May of the following fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers late-filing penalties of 10% to 40% of the tax due plus statutory interest of 0.20% per calendar month for late payment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit is required for a SARL if at the balance-sheet date it meets at least two of the following three thresholds: (i) total balance sheet of EUR 7,112,000; (ii) net turnover (excluding VAT) of EUR 14,224,000; (iii) average workforce of 50 employees during the fiscal year. Below these thresholds, the entity is eligible for an exemption from the appointment of a statutory auditor, unless a shareholder holding at least one-third of the share capital (or where the SARL is under a group, certain other conditions) requests an audit, or where the entity controls or is controlled by other entities. The audit must be conducted by an auditor registered with the Compagnie Nationale des Commissaires aux Comptes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The financial statements must comply with French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan Comptable Général - PCG), which are aligned with French GAAP under the regulations of the Autorité des Normes Comptables (ANC), i.e., regulation ANC 2014-03. The application of IFRS is mandatory only for consolidated financial statements of listed groups; a non-listed SARL may apply French GAAP for its individual financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain a register of beneficial owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) at its registered office and file an annual declaration of beneficial ownership with the RCS via the Guichet Unique within fifteen (15) days of the anniversary date of the original declaration. Any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership, including a share transfer, must be declared within 30 days of the change, and the annual confirmation shall accurately reflect the current ownership structure as of the date of confirmation. The register must contain the name, date and place of birth, nationality, residential address, and percentage of capital held or voting power of each natural person directly or indirectly owning more than 10% of the share capital.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registre des Décisions et des Commissaires aux Comptes)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
Minute Book (Registre des Procès-Verbaux et des Décisions Collectives)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: The annual registered-office provision is typically EUR 250 to EUR 900 (USD 270 to USD 970)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: For a SARL eligible for an exemption from the audit due to size thresholds, the cost is minimal, namely legal fees for the formal request for exemption, typically EUR 300 to EUR 1,200; if a statutory audit is applicable, certified audit fees are typically EUR 4,000 to EUR 12,000 depending on the size and turnover of the entity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (CGI Art. 219-I; fully phased to standard rate as of 1 Jan 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME reduced rate: 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable profit (CGI Art. 219-I-b, turnover ≤ €10m, capital conditions); loss carryforward: indefinite (CGI Art. 209) with annual cap of €1,000,000 + 50% of the excess; optional 1-year carryback credit (CGI Art. 220) refundable after 5 years; CIR research credit 30% (30% on first €100m) — not applicable to pure wholesale trading; no territorial tax holiday for base-metal trading.
